# Choosing a model

**Settings → LLM** in the dashboard decides what answers `$agent`:

| Choice | What answers | Good for |
|---|---|---|
| **Off** | nothing: `$agent` throws `not_configured` | apps that don't use it |
| **Built-in** | a model PocketOne downloads once and runs on your server's CPU | short, focused jobs, with nothing to pay for and nothing leaving your server |
| **API** | your own OpenAI-compatible endpoint, key and model | long answers, chat, the best models |

Until you choose there, `pocketone.yaml` decides: the model its `agent` section names runs built in, and without one
the LLM is off. **Reset to pocketone.yaml** on the same page goes back to it.

## Built-in models

| Model | Download | Memory | Good for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `qwen3-0.6b` | 640 MB | about 1 GB | tags, yes/no, short extraction; the fastest |
| `qwen3-1.7b` | 1.8 GB | about 2 GB | a good default: labels, extraction, short summaries and answers |
| `qwen3-4b` | 2.5 GB | about 3 GB | better answers, slower |

They come from Qwen's own repository and are checked against their SHA-256 when they download. Switching models
downloads the new one and unloads the old one once its answers finish. Nothing downloads for a command such as
`pocketone superuser`; only `serve` starts the model.

The built-in engine is pure Go with tuned assembly for Apple silicon and other ARM CPUs and for x86 (AVX2). It runs
small models about as fast as Ollama does on the CPU, and faster on a one-core server:

| Where | Model | Reading the prompt | Writing the answer |
|---|---|---|---|
| Apple M1 Max, 4 threads | `qwen3-1.7b` (4-bit) | about 140 tokens/s | about 55 tokens/s |
| Apple M1 Max, 4 threads | `qwen3-0.6b` (4-bit) | about 380 tokens/s | about 120 tokens/s |
| 1 vCPU x86 VPS (Skylake) | `qwen3-0.6b` (4-bit) | about 35 tokens/s | about 9 tokens/s |

A word is roughly 1.3 tokens. So on a laptop a short answer takes a second or two; on a one-core server, a label
takes about a second and a paragraph ten or more. Keep answers short with `maxTokens`, and do long jobs in a
[cron](https://pocketbase.io/docs/js-jobs-scheduling/) rather than in a request.

`agent.threads` in `pocketone.yaml` sets how many CPU threads the model uses (default: half your cores), and
`agent.parallel` how many answers it writes at once (default 1; the rest wait their turn). The model also keeps the
start of recent prompts so a repeated preamble isn't read again (`agent.prompt_cache_mb`, see
[Prompt caching](/docs/extensions/agent/prompt-caching)).

## Your own API

Choose **API** and fill in:

- **Endpoint:** the API's base URL with its version: `https://api.openai.com/v1`, `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`,
  `https://api.groq.com/openai/v1`, or `http://localhost:11434/v1` for Ollama on your machine.
- **Key:** your API key. It's never shown again; leave the field empty to keep it. Change the endpoint and you need to
  enter the key again, so a key never goes to a server it wasn't meant for.
- **Model:** the provider's model name, such as `gpt-4o-mini`.

**Test** sends a one-word prompt without saving, and shows the provider's error if there is one.

A `schema` goes to the API as `response_format`, which most providers honor; streaming works with any provider that
streams OpenAI-style.
